text:
sam kim: heads up — bringing up hf/sentencepiece model (hf://foo-spm) for onboarding. after conversion + int8 quant we see decoding drift and token-sequence insertions. suspect token-id gaps (vocab holes) causing KV cache offset issues.

anya patel: steps / commands you used?

sam kim: here's what i ran:
```bash
python tools/convert_spm_to_bpe.py --hf-model hf://foo-spm --out redwood-foo
# exports vocab.txt + merges.txt (we synthesize merges for runtime compatibility)
```

sam kim: tokenizer config in repo had:
```json
{"vocab_size":50304, "special_tokens": {"pad":0, "bos":1, "eos":2}}
```

sam kim: but model embeddings from pytorch are (50305, 512) — off by one.

lina cho: that +1 smells like a removed/added reserved token (e.g. <unk>/<unusedX>) during export.

david rasmussen: if you insert/remove an id anywhere, the runtime's assumption that token ids map directly to positional KV indices breaks — past_key_values indexing will be shifted and all cached KV lookups after the insertion point are wrong.

anya patel: can you show a tiny token-id example where it diverges?

sam kim: repro snippet:
```py
# token ids from tokenizer.encode('Hello there')
expected: [1, 345, 67, 2]
actual:   [1, 345, 68, 67, 2]
# note: extra id 68 inserted between tokens — causes subsequent KV indices to shift by 1
```

sam kim: quant runs on dedicated infra show higher ppl and occasional hallucinations after ~50 tokens. logs attached.

infra-bot: test-run 2024-11-05T14:12Z: started job q8-eval-171800

david rasmussen: common culprits i've seen:
- tokenizer.json special_tokens remapped out-of-order
- sentencepiece vocab export that emits duplicate or gap indices
- a merge-generation script that inserts a placeholder token to satisfy BPE format

anya patel: quick checks to add to onboarding pipeline:
1) assert len(tokenizer) == model.config.vocab_size or raise a warning
2) verify special token ids < len(vocab) and unique
3) diff sentencepiece exported vocab vs final vocab with their indices (no insertions/deletions)

lina cho: small fixer i used locally (very hacky):
```bash
# if embeddings vs vocab off by one, prefer embedding count and remap tokenizer special tokens to available ids
python - <<'PY'
import json
# naive placeholder: inspect pytorch emb shape vs tokenizer config and nudge tokenizer.json
PY
```

sam kim: ran check 1) — config.vocab_size=50304 but len(tokenizer)=50305. so config under-reports. sounds like HF export removed a placeholder but didn't update config.

david rasmussen: actionables:
- conversion script should read embedding matrix rows from model to derive true vocab size if present (model is oracle for emb rows)
- reassign special tokens to lowest unused ids rather than appending mid-vocab
- add token-seq-consistency test: sample prompts -> compare hf tokenizer seq vs exported seq (no insert/delete)

anya patel: also add a small KV-cache smoke test: run short generation with and without caching and compare token-by-token next-token probs.

sam kim: i'll add the tests and a fix to prefer embedding row count as ground truth; plan to remap specials to smallest available ids and emit a conversion report. will open PR within ~2h.

lina cho: also propose adding a quant-eval gate: run 10 short prompts under q8 and compute ppl delta; fail onboarding if delta > 4% relative to fp16 baseline.

anya patel: sounds good. please include the failing examples so we can triage quality regressions quickly. :thumbsup:

sam kim: tagging @david rasmussen for KV cache alignment review — if conversion-side fixes don't remove drift we may need runtime guard (index by positional token order for cache lookups instead of raw id pos).

david rasmussen: indexing by positional order is safer but touches runtime assumptions and perf paths. try conversion fixes first.

infra-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-dev/onboard/foo-spm/171800/logs (q8-eval-171800)

sam kim: thanks all — short-term fix landed in my fork, will open the PR and add the unit tests. will drop links here when ready.

anya patel: great, i'll run the full eval suite once PR is up.

sam kim: will ping. cheers!
